items.text: Stalks detect equality of maps
u,v\colon F\rightrightarrows G\ \text{sheaves}:\quad u=v\iff \forall x:\ u_x=v_x
F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ker(u,v)\iff \forall x:\ F_x\xrightarrow{\sim}\ker(u_x,v_x)
The family $(\mathrm{St}_x)$ is faithful: conservative + commutes with kernels of pairs.
The yoga, again
Exactness statements with finite inverse limits and arbitrary direct limits hold in $\operatorname{Top}(X)$ if they hold in $\mathbf{Sets}$: via presheaves + $a$, or via the fibre functors.
In the modern setting of topoi there may not be enough points: the first argument will still work.
Epimorphisms of sheaves
u\colon F\to G\ \text{epi}\iff \forall x:\ F_x\to G_x\ \text{surjective}
A germ $g_x$ comes from a germ $f_x$: a section of $F$ near $x$ whose image agrees with $g$ near $x$.
Sections of $G$ lift locally, not globally.
F\twoheadrightarrow G\ \not\Longrightarrow\ F(U)\to G(U)\ \text{surjective}
That would be epi in presheaves; epi is a direct-limit notion, different in presheaves and sheaves.
\Gamma(X,F)=F(X)\to\Gamma(X,G)\quad\text{in general not onto}
$X$ compact Hausdorff: onto for every epi only if $X$ totally disconnected.
Cohomology measures the gap between local and global lifting: obstruction.
Algebraic structures on sheaves
Two kinds: those described by inverse limits only; those needing direct limits too.
Structures from inverse limits
$E$ an object of $C$ (with $E\times E$): a composition law.
E\times E\longrightarrow E
Commutative: the swap of $E\times E$ commutes. Likewise associativity, units, inverses.
Units: a final object $\{*\}$; a point of $E$ is a morphism $\{*\}\to E$.
E=e\times E\xrightarrow{\ e\times \mathrm{id}\ }E\times E\xrightarrow{\ m\ }E\quad\text{equals }\mathrm{id}_E
A far nicer way: pass through the functor of points.
E\mapsto E(Z)=\operatorname{Hom}(Z,E),\qquad C\hookrightarrow \hat C\ \text{fully faithful}
\operatorname{Hom}(Z,E\times E)=E(Z)\times E(Z)\longrightarrow E(Z)\quad\text{natural in } Z
A law on $E$ = a law on each set $E(Z)$, functorial in $Z$.
$E$ has the structure (group, monoid, ring, module...) iff each $E(Z)$ does, with the maps $E(Z')\to E(Z)$ morphisms of structures.
No products needed, no diagrams of axioms: transcribe the set-theoretic definition.
Monoid, group, ring, algebra (associative with unit — or Lie, Jordan...), module over a ring or algebra.
These need only finite products (empty one included). A category needs more:
A category inside a category
D_1\overset{s}{\underset{t}{\rightrightarrows}}D_0,\qquad D_1\times_{D_0}D_1\xrightarrow{\ \circ\ }D_1,\qquad \varepsilon\colon D_0\to D_1
Associativity on the threefold fibre product over $D_0$.
Still inverse limits (fibre products).
So: objects $D_0,D_1$ plus, for each $Z$, a category structure on $(D_0(Z),D_1(Z))$, functorial in $Z$.
Also additive categories. Works because $C\to\hat C$ commutes with inverse limits, not direct ones.
And $\operatorname{Top}(X)\subset\hat{\mathcal O}$ commutes with inverse limits.
Sheaves of groups: three views
(1) A sheaf $F$ with a law $F\times F\to F$.
(2) A group structure on each $F(U)$, functorial in $U$.
(3) A functor $\mathcal O^{\circ}\to\mathbf{Groups}$ whose composite with the forgetful functor is a sheaf.
\mathcal O^{\circ}\xrightarrow{\ F\ }\mathbf{Groups}\xrightarrow{\ \text{forget}\ }\mathbf{Sets}\quad\text{a sheaf}
Same for monoids, rings, modules over a sheaf of rings, Lie algebras...
(4) On the fibres: laws $F_x\times F_x\to F_x$, but hard to say that they come from a morphism.
Axioms (isos, monos, equalities) are checked on fibres: the fibre functors are conservative and commute with the limits used.
A left exact functor $U\colon C\to C'$ sends group objects to group objects.
Hence the stalks of a sheaf of groups (rings, ...) are groups (rings, ...).
Structures needing direct limits
Example: comodules. $k$ a ring, $A$ a $k$-coalgebra (coassociative, with counit).
$M$ a $k$-module with a $k$-linear map
M\longrightarrow M\otimes_k A\qquad(\text{plus axioms})
Dual of an $A$-module structure $M\otimes A\to M$ (arrows reversed).
For a group scheme $G$ over $k$ with ring $A$: an action of $G$ on $M$ = a comodule structure.
The tensor product is not an inverse limit: infinite sums and quotient (direct limits).
In sheaves: $k$ a sheaf of rings, $A$ a sheaf of $k$-algebras, $M$ a sheaf of $k$-modules.
M(U)\to M(U)\otimes_{k(U)}A(U)\quad\text{(this does not work)}
Need the tensor product of sheaves; sections do not commute with it.
M(U)\otimes_{k(U)}A(U)\longrightarrow (M\otimes_k A)(U)\quad\text{not bijective}
Must give $M\to M\otimes_kA$ as a map of sheaves, not on sections: construct the sheaf tensor product internally.
Torsors
$G$ a group acting on a set $E$. $E$ is a torsor (principal space) under $G$ if
E\neq\varnothing\quad\text{and}\quad \forall x,y\in E\ \ \exists!\, g\in G:\ y=gx
The second condition alone does not give the first ($E$ empty).
